Acclamato dalla critica per svariate ragioni, hereditary si rivela in realtà un’opera fine a se stessa. Nonostante la cura dell’immagine e della fotografia che ne fa da padrona, la resa estetica non è neanche fatta così bene se messa a paragone con la fotografia e la cura dei film di Dario Argento. È un film vuoto e quasi noioso, incapace di generare la paura e l’ansia che rappresentano le vere colonne portanti del cinema horror. Negli ultimi anni ci si focalizza fin troppo sull’"elevated horror", e qui se ne fa un uso così abbondante da perdere di vista l’origine stessa per cui questi film sono nati. All’inizio l’opera si camuffa da dramma psicologico, per poi sfociare in un finale tremendo che cade sul fasullo e sulla scelta demoniaca, finendo inevitabilmente per scivolare nel ridicolo.

To be fair, the acting is good and the script's individual plot points are okay on paper, but the execution falls flat. It ends up feeling painfully slow and very boring throughout.

I wish I could like Hereditary more. It attempts to tap into a fear not engaged with enough: that is, hereditable disease/mental illness. Formerly, such diseases were incorporated into horror in a mystical or religious way, birth defects being a prime example. Such defects were alternatively viewed as divine or a curse, either being an elevation from normal existence. Now (by that I mean at least since the modern synthesis), with the scientific comphrension of herediability, a new sort of horror has arose. The horror of potentially damning your offspring to a life of suffering, though by no personal fault of your own. In this film, some scenes capture this anxity brilliantly, both from the mom and her son's perspective. Unfortunately, these scenes are invariably undermined by less-than-great acting or by being retroactively neutured (e.g. made into a dream). Even if the individual scene was allowed to breath (rarely), the overarching themes (doll-house, A24 etc), which weren't pulled together well, hampered the cinematography. I did like that the family (namely the father) was supportive, the "curse" of disease can strike anyone. The ending was also provocative (especially when read through the lens of mental illness). Also, maybe its just me (or that I had this movie partially spoiled), but it really wasn't that scary! Probably because it felt so pastiche?

A symphony of gimmicks and muddied waters. I hate to be that person again…. but I genuinely didn’t enjoy this at all. For me, possession/satanic cults and rituals as a trope usually lead to something, to some greater overarching plot. And although not everything needs to have a deeply moving message, this movie unfortunately feels like it lost its own in the process. A lot of the more memorable and twisted scenes only work and have the impact they do because they leverage that early gravitas of the potential exploration of grief, lose of youth/bodily autonomy, familial cycles and traumas, etc. But this film never truly makes that turn around back to the point it initially latched onto and conveniently lets go for the sake of shock factor. I’ll totally be the person to give the actors their flowers, and some of the scenes would not have functioned as such great pieces of storytelling if it was not for the camerawork. But aesthetics and talents can only take you so far. I think this has consistently been my gripe with Ari Aster is he has such great ideas and his attention to detail is insane, but are his grandiose projects fleshed out to begin with? Honestly no. He relies on the conversation and pushing the limits of what horror can be, which I do frankly respect him for; but again this, like a lot of his other work let me go as easily as it grabbed me. And genuinely I’m left with 0 takeaway from this… maybe I’m the problem

The lore is insane even though most people don’t realize there is any lore. I’m pretty sure it’s based off the Lesser Key of Solomon, which is pseudepigrapha, meaning writing attributed to a biblical figure that was deemed false by the church. The mysteries go deeper as the movie progresses and the lore unravels. You eventually realize that this normal family is involved with so much more than we realized. The soundtrack is good too.
